stories.title: Berkshire Residential Takes Full Ownership of Multifamily Mortgage Lender MF1
stories.excerpt: Boston-based Berkshire Residential Investments has agreed to acquire Limekiln Real Estate Investment Management, LP’s 50% interest in MF1 Process LLC, making Berkshire the sole owner of the private-label multifamily mortgage lender. MF1 was launched in 2018 as a 50/50 joint venture between Limekiln founder Scott Waynebern and Berkshire. Terms were not disclosed. As part of the transaction, it is anticipated that most Limekiln employees will become Berkshire employees. Eric Draeger, partner and Berkshire’s CIO, said, “We are thrilled to welcome the Limekiln team into the Berkshire family. The joint venture that we formed eight years ago with Limekiln has been very successful and we are pleased to now have fully integrated multifamily equity, securities and debt origination platforms. We look forward to serving our investors and borrowers as one Berkshire team.” Berkshire Global Advisors is serving as financial advisor and Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher LLP as legal advisor to Berkshire Residential Investments. Herbert Smith Freehills Kramer (US) LLP is acting as legal advisor to Limekiln Real Estate. Waynebern will remain CEO of Limekiln, which will focus on building a new CRE strategy outside of multifamily debt. Pictured: Berkshire Residential headquarters at One Beacon St., Boston. bullets: Berkshire Residential acquires Limekiln's 50% stake in MF1 mortgage lender; becomes sole owner.
MF1 originated as 2018 JV; now fully integrates equity, securities, debt platforms under Berkshire.
Limekiln CEO Waynebern remains; pivots firm to non-multifamily CRE debt strategy.
stories.summary: Berkshire Residential has taken full ownership of MF1 Process LLC, a private-label multifamily mortgage lender, by acquiring Limekiln Real Estate Investment Management's 50% stake. The deal consolidates Berkshire's multifamily equity, securities, and debt origination under one roof. Limekiln founder Scott Waynebern stays as CEO but shifts the firm's strategy away from multifamily debt.
stories.impact: Vertical integration of debt origination under Berkshire strengthens their competitive position in multifamily underwriting and may signal confidence in market conditions. Consolidation of lending platforms reduces fragmentation in the private-label MF lending space; watch for whether this signals Berkshire's intent to finance more of their own developments or tighten origination standards across the platform.

stories.title: Albion Residential, Clayco Reach Milestone for St. Louis Apartment Project
stories.excerpt: Albion Residential and Clayco announced that Albion West End reached its topping-out milestone. This marks the completion of the building’s structural frame, which is a significant step toward delivering the 30-story luxury residential tower to St. Louis’ Central West End on schedule, with first residents expected to be welcomed in spring and full completion of the tower in the summer of 2027. Located at 4974 Lindell Boulevard, Albion West End has begun to transform the St. Louis skyline by serving as a gateway to the Central West End. The development is being delivered by a best-in-class team that, in addition to Albion and Clayco, also includes developer Koplar Properties, design firm LJC, façade partner Ventana, and Concrete Strategies. When complete, Albion West End will feature 305 luxury residences ranging from studios to three-bedroom homes, along with ground-floor retail. Residents will enjoy a resort-style pool deck, rooftop terrace with panoramic city views, and hospitality-inspired amenity spaces designed to foster connection and well-being. Where the apartment industry connects. Meet the owners, investors, developers, lenders, brokers, and service providers driving today’s multifamily market at Connect Apartments. Build relationships, uncover opportunities, and stay ahead of what’s next. The post Albion Residential, Clayco Reach Milestone for St. Louis Apartment Project appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Albion Residential, Clayco top out 305-unit luxury tower in St. Louis Central West End.
Albion West End reaches structural completion; opens spring 2027, full finish summer 2027.
30-story development includes studios to 3BR, resort pool, rooftop terrace, ground retail.
stories.summary: Albion Residential and Clayco have reached structural topping-out on Albion West End, a 30-story, 305-unit luxury residential tower at 4974 Lindell Boulevard in St. Louis's Central West End. The project is on schedule for spring 2027 occupancy and summer 2027 full completion. Units range from studios to three-bedroom homes, with ground-floor retail and premium amenities including a resort-style pool and rooftop terrace.
stories.impact: Completion of institutional-quality supply in Central West End ahead of 2027 absorption window signals confidence in St. Louis luxury rental demand and validates that submarket's transformation. Developers should monitor absorption and pricing to assess whether gateway projects like this absorb demand or signal market saturation in the Central West End corridor.

stories.title: Lower Manhattan Has Undergone “Profound Transformation” Since 9/11
stories.excerpt: A quarter-century after the Sept. 11 terror attacks, Lower Manhattan has undergone “a profound transformation,” New York State Comptroller Thomas DiNapoli said in a report charting the area’s socioeconomic changes. DiNapoli cited a diversified business community, an expanding tourism sector, major public transportation investments and the emergence of a 24-hour neighborhood that has seen the number of housing units and residents more than double since 2000. Lower Manhattan’s population has increased from 32,446 in 2000 to 70,761 in 2024, outpacing Manhattan overall. The increase, concentrated across the Financial District and Tribeca, was supported by a jump in housing from 21,337 units in 2002 to 46,194 as 2026 began, driven by zoning changes and the conversions of office buildings for residential and ground-floor retail use. “Twenty-five years ago, it was impossible to imagine the neighborhoods around Ground Zero looking like they do today,” DiNapoli said. “Lower Manhattan rose from those ashes with an enormous amount of effort and investment. Today, the growing population, the mix of retail, business and government offices, as well as hotels, restaurants and cultural destinations, speak to New York’s and America’s tenacity in the wake of one of the darkest days in our history.” The post Lower Manhattan Has Undergone “Profound Transformation” Since 9/11 appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Lower Manhattan population grew from 32,446 (2000) to 70,761 (2024); 118% increase.
Housing units rose from 21,337 (2002) to 46,194 (2026); zoning changes, office conversions drove supply.
Financial District and Tribeca concentrated growth; 24-hour neighborhood with diversified business, tourism, transit investment.
stories.summary: New York State Comptroller DiNapoli's report documents Lower Manhattan's transformation since 9/11: population more than doubled from 32,446 to 70,761 since 2000, while housing stock grew from 21,337 units in 2002 to 46,194 by early 2026. Growth concentrated in Financial District and Tribeca, fueled by zoning reforms and office-to-residential conversions. The area now supports a 24-hour neighborhood with diversified commerce, hospitality, and major transit investment.
stories.impact: Office conversion pipeline and zoning flexibility in Lower Manhattan remain a proven demand engine; however, the doubling of housing supply since 2002 signals that new ground-up multifamily development now faces elevated competition from adaptive reuse. Developers eyeing Lower Manhattan should prioritize underutilized office assets or constrained sites in Financial District/Tribeca submarkets where conversion economics still favor new supply over conversion.

stories.title: Apparel Manufacturer Bagatelle International Takes 24K SF at 463 Seventh Avenue
stories.excerpt: Canadian fashion brand and apparel manufacturer Bagatelle International is relocating to a full-floor lease at 463 Seventh Avenue. The 23,785-square-foot deal is the largest of two new office leases at the Arsenal Company’s Garment District tower between West 35th and West 36th streets. The transactions span a collective 33,083 square feet and bring the 22-story building to full occupancy, according to landlord brokers Adams & Company. Asking rent for both deals was $59 per square foot. “Bringing 463 Seventh Avenue to 100 percent leased is another milestone for our portfolio and a testament to the resilience of the Midtown office market,” Adams & Company’s David Levy, who represented the landlord in both deals alongside Benjamin Levy, said in a statement. Bagatelle International, known for its high-end apparel brands Bagatelle and Avec Les Filles, signed on at 463 Seventh Avenue in mid-June, taking the entire 10th floor. Lee & Associates NYC’s Dennis Someck and Justin Myers negotiated on behalf of Bagatelle. The company plans to relocate its offices and showroom in October from a smaller space at Brause Realty’s 141 West 36th Street, where it currently occupies several floors, according to Someck. “I’ve represented Bagatelle for some 25 years, relocating them and expanding them multiple times,” Someck told Commercial Observer. “So I’ve watched them grow over the years to a much larger and meaningful tenant, and this was an opportunity to take them into the next transition.” The second lease deal at the Garment District tower was inked in late July by KS Engineers, a full-service engineering and construction management firm based in Newark, N.J. The firm, also known as KSE, took 9,298 square feet for general and executive office use. KSE was represented by CBRE’s Alexander Benisatto, Carolyn Sica and Trevor Larkin. bullets: Bagatelle International leases 23,785 SF at 463 Seventh Avenue, Garment District; $59/SF.

stories.summary: Canadian apparel brand Bagatelle International signed a full-floor lease of 23,785 square feet at 463 Seventh Avenue in Manhattan's Garment District at $59 per square foot. The deal, plus a second lease, brought the Arsenal Company's 22-story tower to 100% occupancy. Bagatelle, known for high-end brands, took the entire 10th floor in mid-June.
stories.impact: Limited relevance to multifamily. Office lease activity in Midtown reflects marginal stabilization, but does not signal demand drivers (job growth, employer relocation) that would cascade into multifamily absorption. Monitor if Garment District office stabilization eventually unlocks conversion opportunities into residential stock.

stories.title: Sagard Real Estate Acquires Tukwila Industrial Property
stories.excerpt: Sagard Real Estate has acquired 1100 Andover Park West, a 133,750-square-foot industrial property in Tukwila, Washington, within the greater Seattle market. Located at the northern end of the Kent Valley, the property sits on approximately 5.6 acres in one of the Puget Sound region’s most established infill industrial corridors. The location provides access to Interstate 5, Interstate 405 and State Route 167, as well as Seattle-Tacoma International Airport, the Port of Seattle and major population centers throughout the region. The fully leased property is occupied by a national wholesale distributor that has operated at the site for more than 25 years. The facility features 24-foot clear heights, 16 dock-high loading doors and four points of ingress and egress, providing flexibility to serve a broader range of warehouse, distribution and industrial users. “1100 Andover Park West is a prime example of the functional, well-located properties we continue to target in infill industrial markets,” said Tom Stover, Managing Director, Acquisitions at Sagard Real Estate. stories.summary: Sagard Real Estate has acquired 1100 Andover Park West, a fully leased 133,750-square-foot industrial property on 5.6 acres in Tukwila, Washington, in the Puget Sound's Kent Valley infill corridor. The facility, occupied by a long-tenured national wholesale distributor, offers 24-foot clear heights, 16 dock-high doors, and proximity to I-5, I-405, SeaTac Airport, and the Port of Seattle.
stories.impact: Not directly relevant to multifamily. However, industrial acquisition in Puget Sound infill confirms investor appetite for constrained-supply logistics corridors near Seattle metro; watch for whether port/airport-proximate industrial land intensification crowds out nearby multifamily entitlements or increases local construction cost/labor competition.

stories.title: Draper and Kramer Closes $94M Refinance for Fulton Market Multifamily Property
stories.excerpt: Draper and Kramer, Incorporated’s Bill Barry and Bill Stewart, both senior vice presidents with the firm’s Commercial Finance Group, have closed a $93.5 million refinance loan on behalf of Sterling Bay and Ascentris for The Elizabeth, a 28-story multifamily tower at 225 N. Elizabeth St. in Chicago’s Fulton Market. “This deal is indicative of the strength of the multifamily market here in Chicago, where limited new inventory continues to drive rents at existing properties. It also demonstrates the appetite non-agency lenders have for financing high-quality multifamily deals,” said Barry. Completed in 2024, the property includes 350 rental apartments and 10,000 square feet of street-level retail space. “Fulton Market is a high-velocity pocket that illustrates how the financing landscape is easing for the right opportunities in prime locations,” added Stewart. “That extends to refinance situations like The Elizabeth, where our clients were looking to swap out their current rate, as well as construction financing for new projects in areas where multifamily demand is growing.” If you’re reading about the multifamily industry, you should be in the room with its leaders. Connect Apartments brings together the executives featured in Connect CRE’s coverage for an afternoon of high-level insights and unmatched networking on September 22 at The Biltmore in LA. bullets: Draper and Kramer close $93.5M refinance for The Elizabeth, 350-unit Fulton Market tower.
Non-agency lenders financing high-quality multifamily; 2024-completed, 28-story property with 10K SF retail.

stories.summary: Draper and Kramer have closed a $93.5 million refinance loan on behalf of Sterling Bay and Ascentris for The Elizabeth, a 28-story, 350-unit multifamily tower completed in 2024 at 225 N. Elizabeth Street in Chicago's Fulton Market. The deal demonstrates non-agency lender appetite for high-quality multifamily in prime locations. Fulton Market is characterized as a supply-constrained, high-velocity pocket driving rent growth at existing properties.
stories.impact: Refinance execution on stabilized 2024 delivery signals non-agency lending has normalized for trophy Chicago multifamily assets. Fulton Market's description as supply-constrained validates scarcity premium; developers should prioritize remaining Fulton Market entitlements and adjacent Pilsen/Near West Side parcels where land cost and regulatory barriers remain lower than core Market district but absorption patterns confirm spillover demand.

stories.title: Two Supermarkets Ink Deals Along Brooklyn’s Atlantic Avenue
stories.excerpt: Two new supermarkets are coming to Atlantic Avenue in Prospect Heights, Brooklyn. The grocers will arrive at two of EMP Capital Group’s newly developed residential projects two blocks apart at 880 Atlantic Avenue and 1042 Atlantic Avenue, Commercial Observer has learned. In the largest deal, CTown Supermarkets signed a 20-year lease for 8,400 square feet at the base of the 19-story, 237-unit 1042 Atlantic Avenue, also known as Prosper Brooklyn, which was completed this year. Meanwhile, a new grocer named Atlantic Market inked a 20-year, 8,000-square-foot deal on the ground floor of the 19-story, 257-unit 880 Atlantic Avenue, also known as Eight80 BK, which was completed last year. The leases were signed Aug. 15, and both supermarkets are set to open during the third quarter of 2027, according to broker MOD Commercial Realty. Both of the new supermarkets are independently owned and operated. The asking rent for each deal was $50 per square foot. Mod’s Eddie Mamiye, Meyer Dagmy and Mike Sutton represented both sides in each deal. Spokespeople for EMP Capital and CTown did not immediately respond to requests for comment, while a spokesperson for Atlantic Market could not be reached for comment. In both developments, EMP Capital used New York City’s Food Retail Expansion to Support Health (FRESH) program, an initiative that uses zoning benefits and tax incentives to allow developers to build slightly larger buildings in underserved neighborhoods if they include a qualifying grocery store. Prosper Brooklyn and Eight80 BK also both went up as part of the Atlantic Avenue Mixed-Use Plan, which was approved by the New York City Council in May 2025 and allowed denser housing development within a roughly 21-block stretch of Atlantic Avenue. The plan is designed to foster the development of approximately 4,600 new apartments, including 1,900 income-restricted homes. “Thousands of new units are coming to the neighborhood with the Atlantic Avenue rezoning. Both leases are at $50/SF and open Q3 2027.
stories.impact: Anchor grocery tenants finalizing leases 2–3 years post-residential delivery signals strong residential absorption and neighborhood demand maturity in Prospect Heights. The ability to attract independent grocers at $50/SF validates that recent multifamily supply here is sticky and supportive of neighborhood-scale retail. Developers eyeing nearby underutilized sites should model for similar anchors and note Prospect Heights' shift toward higher density mixed-use.

stories.title: S3 Capital Lends $45M to Build Williamsburg Apartments on Church Land
stories.excerpt: A Brooklyn developer got a higher calling for its latest multifamily project. David Grunfeld, through the entity GW Infinity, has landed $45 million of construction financing to build a 99-unit apartment building with an affordable housing component at a church-affiliated site in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, Commercial Observer can first report, S3 Capital provided the leasehold construction loan for the development of the 17-story complex at 277 North Eighth Street, which will have 20 percent of the units designated as affordable under New York City’s 485-x tax incentive program. Grunfeld filed plans in December 2025 to demolish a vacant two-story building at the property that sits on land controlled through a long-term ground lease with the Roman Catholic Church of Our Lady of Mount Carmel, CO first reported at the time. Shawn Safdie, head of origination at S3 Capital, noted that the unconventional transaction involved structuring the loan around the leasehold interest and the terms of the ground lease to enable the borrower to proceed with construction without the capital commitment typically required for acquiring the underlying land outright. “This loan is a great example of S3 Capital’s ability to structure creative financing solutions for complex real estate transactions,” Safdie said in a statement. “This is our fifth loan with this sponsorship team in this neighborhood, so we deeply understand the market and the nuances of developing here.” Robert Schwartz, a co-founder and managing principal at S3 Capital, said the deal underscores S3’s “development background” to allow it to be “creative in structuring tailored solutions” for the “specific needs of a project.” The property is three blocks from the Bedford Avenue L train station with mass transit access into Manhattan. bullets: S3 Capital lends $45M construction financing for 99-unit apartment project in Williamsburg, Brooklyn.

stories.summary: S3 Capital has provided $45 million in construction financing to David Grunfeld's GW Infinity for a 99-unit, 17-story apartment development at 277 North Eighth Street in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, on a Roman Catholic Church ground lease. Twenty percent of units (approximately 20) are designated affordable under NYC's 485-x tax incentive. The loan was structured around the leasehold interest and ground lease terms to enable project feasibility.
stories.impact: Success of leasehold financing structure on church ground lease in Williamsburg validates that non-traditional ownership arrangements can access debt capital, unlocking constrained institutional land for multifamily. This expands addressable development sites in tight Williamsburg; watch for similar church/institutional ground-lease transactions to proliferate in Brooklyn as developers seek constrained land and lenders gain comfort with structured leasehold products.

stories.title: Coney Island Prep Inks 45K-SF Deal to Relocate to 773 Neptune Avenue
stories.excerpt: Coney Island Preparatory Public Charter School is moving from its Gravesend, Brooklyn, location to none other than Coney Island. The school signed a 39-year condominium leasehold agreement to build a 45,190-square-foot high school at Elie Fouerti’s 773 Neptune Avenue, where it will grow to accommodate 500 students when it opens for enrollment in summer 2027, according to tenant broker Open Impact Real Estate. The new school is being developed by Rybak Development. Asking rent for the building was not disclosed, but the average office asking rent borough-wide was $51.01 per square foot in the second quarter of 2026, according to a Cushman & Wakefield report. The average retail asking rent throughout Brooklyn was $55.02 per square foot over the same period, according to a report from Matthews Real Estate Investment Services, citing CoStar data. “This project gives Coney Island Prep the room and resources to keep pace with its students’ ambitions,” Alexander Smith, senior vice president at Open Impact, said in a statement. “We set out to find a long-term, affordable solution that would reflect the school’s mission and strengthen its presence in the Coney Island community. Securing this off-market opportunity will allow Coney Island Prep to expand its enrollment and deliver purpose-built facilities for years to come.” Smith represented the school alongside Open Impact’s Stephen Powers, while Fouerti Realty used in-house representation. Fouerti Realty did not immediately respond to a request for comment. “This isn’t just a building — it’s a statement about what our scholars deserve,” Karen Johnson, CEO of Coney Island Prep, said in a statement. “The facilities we’re gaining, from purpose-built labs to a full gymnasium to a kitchen that feeds our entire network, are designed to meet our scholars where they are today and grow with them into the future.” It’s unclear whether the new Coney Island Prep school is part of a larger development going up on t
bullets: Coney Island Prep signs 39-year leasehold for 45,190 SF high school at 773 Neptune Avenue.
Charter school relocates from Gravesend; capacity 500 students; opens summer 2027.
Elie Fouerti development; no rent disclosed; comparable office $51/SF, retail $55/SF borough-wide Q2 2026.
stories.summary: Coney Island Preparatory Public Charter School has signed a 39-year leasehold agreement to occupy 45,190 square feet of a new high school facility at 773 Neptune Avenue in Coney Island, Brooklyn, developed by Elie Fouerti. The school will relocate from Gravesend and open for enrollment in summer 2027 with capacity for 500 students. Rent terms were not disclosed.
stories.impact: Not directly relevant to multifamily. However, institutional education anchor in Coney Island signals long-term neighborhood stabilization investment; watch for whether charter school success and year-round foot traffic catalyze adjacent residential infill or prompt municipal investment in Coney Island infrastructure, which could unlock multifamily development in currently underutilized blocks near the boardwalk.

stories.title: Affinius Capital, Axonic Capital Lend $48M for Suburban Boston Apartments Build
stories.excerpt: A Boston development firm’s plan for a multifamily project in suburban Boston is proving dino-mite. Dinosaur Capital Partners has landed $48 million of construction financing to build a multifamily property in Lexington, Mass., Commercial Observer has learned. Affinius Capital and Axonic Capital originated the loan for Dinosaur’s 130-unit apartment project at 7 Hartwell Avenue in Lexington near Westview Cemetery. “Lexington is a supply-constrained, high-barrier suburb where new institutional-quality housing is in short supply,” David Greenburg, co-head of debt originations at Affinius Capital, said in a statement. “This financing supports the ground-up development of a Class A multifamily property in one of Greater Boston’s more established suburban markets.” Located 14 miles northwest of Downtown Boston, the five-story multifamily complex will consist of 110 market-rate apartments and 20 units designated as affordable housing. The property will include 400 square feet of retail space along with amenities such as a fitness center, yoga studio and a coworking lounge. The loan was closed nearly a year to the date after Affinius and Axonic kicked off a strategic partnership aimed at fostering mid-market first mortgage financing for new development projects. The lenders have now done six transactions since the inaugural deal closed for a Long Island self-storage campus in September 2015. “The Boston metro region continues to see high demand, creating opportunities to pair flexible financing with experienced developers,” Erik Nygaard, principal and portfolio manager at Axonic Capital, said in a statement. Dinosaur Capital Partners did not immediately return a request for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Affinius Capital, Axonic Capital lend $48M construction financing for Dinosaur Capital Partners multifamily build.
130-unit project at 7 Hartwell Avenue, Lexington, MA; 110 market-rate, 20 affordable units.
5-story complex 14 miles NW of Downtown Boston; supply-constrained, high-barrier suburb; 400 SF retail.
stories.summary: Affinius Capital and Axonic Capital have originated a $48 million construction loan for Dinosaur Capital Partners' 130-unit multifamily project at 7 Hartwell Avenue in Lexington, Massachusetts, 14 miles northwest of Downtown Boston. The five-story complex includes 110 market-rate units and 20 affordable units, plus 400 square feet of retail. Lexington is characterized as a supply-constrained, high-barrier suburb with limited new institutional-quality housing.
stories.impact: Construction financing execution on supply-constrained suburban Boston site validates non-agency lender appetite for Class A rental housing in high-barrier suburbs. Lexington's supply scarcity and NW Boston suburban tier positioning suggest strong fundamental demand; developers should prioritize remaining Boston-area suburban entitlements, especially near transit corridors, as affordable housing mandates and zoning continue to favor mixed-income new supply in constrained outer metros.
